articles.title: Sadie Sandler to Star in Netflix Horror Movie 'Malibu' From Vertigo, Happy Madison (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Room 101 also produces director Tod "Kip" Williams' feature about a dog-sitting gig gone wrong.
articles.content:
Sadie Sandler is set to make a splash as she prepares to star in her first horror movie.

The actress, who recently led the Netflix comedy Roommates , will collaborate again with the streamer on the horror feature Malibu , The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Tod "Kip" Williams, known for helming Paranormal Activity 2 , is set to direct the film from a script he wrote with Tom Pabst, who worked on the superhero series Titans .

Malibu centers on Sadie Sandler as an aspiring actress who accepts a last-minute dog-sitting job at a reclusive movie star's Malibu mansion. Soon, she learns that the house is not what she expected.

While Sandler appeared in Netflix's 2020 spooky comedy Hubie Halloween opposite dad Adam Sandler and has voiced a role in Sony Pictures' animated Hotel Transylvania franchise, Malibu is described as straight horror and is said to carry a much different tone from her previous projects.

Sadie Sandler recently appeared on Netflix's Nobody Wants This , and her feature credits include Roommates , Jay Kelly , Happy Gilmore 2 and You Are So Not Invited to My Bat Mitzvah .

In addition to helming Paranormal Activity 2 , Williams directed John Cusack and Samuel L. Jackson in the 2016 movie Cell that adapted Stephen King's sci-fi horror novel.

Lee, who was named THR' s producer of the year in 2025, has served as executive producer on such horror series as Peacock's Crystal Lake and HBO's It: Welcome to Derry . His recent feature credits include Resident Evil , Weapons , A Minecraft Movie and Obsession director Curry Barker's forthcoming movie Anything but Ghosts .

articles.title: Why Did Netflix Cancel Mindhunter? David Fincher Breaks Silence on Ending (And What Can Bring It Back)
articles.summary: Throw a rock on the internet and the answer to "What's the best Netflix show ever" will no doubt bring up Mindhunter, the psychological thriller drama series from David Fincher that only lasted two seasons on the streaming platform. Even though in the years since that show went off the air, Netflix has produced plenty […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Throw a rock on the internet and the answer to " What's the best Netflix show ever " will no doubt bring up Mindhunter , the psychological thriller drama series from David Fincher that only lasted two seasons on the streaming platform . Even though in the years since that show went off the air, Netflix has produced plenty of Emmy-winning shows that have been watched for billions of minutes, Mindhunter remains a fixture of their legacy as a TV studio . Billed as being a show with a five-season plan, and the seeds already being set up across the earliest episodes to reveal the show's full arc, Mindhunter was cut short and fans have been asking for more ever since.

David Fincher stopped by the Happy Sad Confused podcast recently, where he opened up about the ending of Mindhunter at Netflix , confirming the myriad reasons why the show didn't continue at the streamer and what fans can do to get the show back (he's only being 98% facetious). In short, the answer is cost and time. "I love the fact that people finally love the show. I'm not scolding. I'm just saying things have a time and a place," Fincher said. "And the best-laid plans led to not an optimal delivery system or schedule. And getting off on that wrong foot put us on the wrong foot for the second season… And I just said, 'I don't understand what those concessions (with Netflix) would be that would grow an audience from 2 million to what? Ten? Twelve? What does it need to be?"

Fincher got into the nitty-gritty of what went into the development and the production for Mindhunter in its first season, confirming that trouble in the early days of filming Season 1 led to the delays that would end up hurting the show completely. The filmmaker noted that working in the traditional structure of a TV writers' room led to troubles with the initial scripts.

"The first season, which I'm very happy with, I was proud of, and we did the best we could and I was learning…I really felt like Mindhunter could do for the things that I had tried to do in Zodiac , could do it in a lab setting, in an interesting petri dish," Fincher said, but lamented that he became the de facto showrunner of the series despite not having that title. "It is so much work. That show was a 90-hour work week when I wasn't directing. And I'm not afraid of a lot of work; to me it's like that's how I know I'm alive when I'm at work. But that first season was a cluster f*ck."

Fincher went on to reveal that while they were filming Season 1 of Mindhunter , a showrunner ("that Netflix really liked, had a great reputation," according to Fincher) and a team of writers were hired to begin developing scripts for Season 2. Since the director was so knee-deep in the series at the time, Fincher didn't have a chance to read them until eight or nine episodes had been written.

"I read these scripts, and I threw them away. It was not our show," Fincher added. "So then it was a mad scramble to, 'Okay, we're starting over; we've got to get eight to ten.' I wanted to have 10 in my pocket before we started shooting. I think we got eight and it was the same kind of clusterf*ck the second time."

Fincher went on to estimate that throwing out the scripts for Season 2 "cost us almost a year," meaning that the gap between seasons for Mindhunter would grow from at least a year to 18 or 19 months. At the end of work on Season 2 of Mindhunter , it appeared like that time between seasons was going to grow to two years before Season 3 might be released. Though major gaps between seasons have become the norm in Hollywood ( Stranger Things took three years between Seasons 3 and 4, and another three between Seasons 4 & 5), at the time Netflix was still making annual seasons for its shows.

"That's when Netflix said, 'Look, we got to be honest with you, there are two million people who love the show, and the show cost $100 million a season. It's basically guys with styrofoam cups in their hands sitting at stainless steel tables getting the rundown. Is there anything you can do so this audience can grow?' And I said, 'What do you mean?'"

Fincher revealed that Netflix asked if changes to Mindhunter could be made, such as making it "closer to CSI " or perhaps find a way to add scenes where "they run after somebody with a gun in their hand." True to his word, Fincher wouldn't make those changes, but as we know, that helped bring the show to an end.

"I said, 'No, I can't. I won't. And I don't think you really want me to.' And they said, 'We don't, but we don't know how else how else are we going to grow this?' So, every time somebody says to me, 'Can’t we bring that back?' I say, 'Here's what I need you to do. You need to go out, you need to make 10 million friends, and you need each of them to send me $10, and then I'll do it."

articles.title: FCC To Vote On Plan To Relax Local TV And Radio Ownership Limits
articles.summary: The FCC plans to vote next month on a proposal to further relax ownership limits on broadcasters, this time targeting a rule that limits the number of stations a company can own in one market. The proposal would allow for TV and radio broadcasters to exceed those limits on a case-by-case basis and if the […]
articles.content:
The FCC plans to vote next month on a proposal to further relax ownership limits on broadcasters, this time targeting a rule that limits the number of stations a company can own in one market.

The proposal would allow for TV and radio broadcasters to exceed those limits on a case-by-case basis and if the agency determines that it will "promote the public interest," with criteria including diversity and localism. Currently, a company can own up to two stations in the same market.

If the proposal is adopted, companies would no longer have to abide by the "subcaps" that restrict the balance of FM and AM stations they own in a market. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Donald Trump Puts Himself At Center Of Jensen Huang's Reinstatement, Downplays "Sex Sells" Scandal Amid National Security Concerns News Democratic National Committee Plans 12 Presidential Primary Debates Starting In June

The proposal is the latest effort to modify ownership rules under chairman Brendan Carr , who has said that he wanted to increase the leverage of local stations compared to national networks. The FCC proposal would keep in place a rule that prohibits any one entity from owning two broadcast networks. Last summer, the FCC voted to abandon a rule that limits a company from collectively owning stations covering more than 39% of the country.

Carr wrote in a blog post that the change is needed because the "media marketplace has changed dramatically in recent years, yet many FCC regulations remain stuck in the past."

He wrote, "This item completes a long overdue effort to modernize those local broadcast ownership rules so that local TV and radio stations can continue to compete into the future. This will empower local broadcasters to grow stronger, invest in their communities, and deliver the news and information Americans rely on every day."

An FCC official denied that the vote on the proposal had to do with the change in control in Congress, with Democrats holding substantial majorities starting in January.

When the FCC approved Nexstar's merger with Tegna last March, it granted a waiver to allow the combined company to control more than two stations in a number of markets. articles.title: 4 Incredible Non-Rockstar Games That Influenced GTA 6 and Are Still Worth Playing
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games Rockstar Games has delivered a truly incredible title in Grand Theft Auto 6, creating a life-like world whose immersive quality builds off past GTA series games and the Red Dead Redemption franchise. While the best parts of Rockstar's best hits certainly played a part in GTA 6's direction, there are other great titles that have […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Rockstar Games has delivered a truly incredible title in Grand Theft Auto 6 , creating a life-like world whose immersive quality builds off past GTA series games and the Red Dead Redemption franchise. While the best parts of Rockstar's best hits certainly played a part in GTA 6 's direction, there are other great titles that have come out over the last 13 years that also could have inspired Rockstar's design philosophies. From putting weight and consequences onto player choices to the overall aesthetic of GTA 6 's Miami-inspired Vice City and Leonida, there are some stellar games that helped bring GTA 6 to life.

Games outside of the Rockstar bubble have always been influential to the GTA series, such as how the Max Payne , Saints Row , or Mafia series all had elements of gameplay Rockstar adopted into their flagship franchise. At the same time, those series borrowed concepts from GTA or Red Dead Redemption , creating a healthy ecosystem of shared game creativity within unique spaces. However, a game doesn't need to have a semi open-world sandbox with crime and chaos to inspire GTA back, as other ideas can be seen in GTA 6 from unlikely sources.

One such unlikely source of inspiration for GTA 6 is Kingdom Come: Deliverance , as well as its sequel. While Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 came out in 2025, only a year before GTA 6 , its predecessor established much of that series signature immersive RPG depth, within a historical fantasy setting often used to tell a fantastical story of some kind. Almost taking the direct opposite route, the Kingdom Come: Deliverance games started in 2018 with a title that almost took the term "grounded approach" to an extreme. Players had to truly work their way up in every sense of the word, turning an illiterate main character into someone competent step by step.

The famous part of the Kingdom Come: Deliverance games is how every action has some sort of consequence, whether for better or worse. For example, you could choose to engage with a particular quest, but if you forget about it, the people involved in it could die off-screen in a few days. Similarly, you have to eat, drink, sleep, and perform basic physical health activities to keep your stats up, requiring a level of maintenance for your character that most RPGs fear doing. You may notice that a version of a physical health mechanic in GTA 6 does practically the same thing, revealing this inspiration in an obvious fashion.

Most of Kingdom Come: Deliverance is non-linear as well, with players have to go out into the world and figure out what they're going to do as they travel. Much like GTA games, players who commit crimes in certain regions will be hunted, making that non-linear travel more complicated. Reputation plays a big factor in this RPG series, and it is something players might notice is more emphasized in GTA 6 than it has been in past games. The Heat system in particular from GTA 6 reflects the design of Kingdom Come: Deliverance in some ways, creating a greater sense of immersion by having the player's impact on the world be felt at every step.

The map design of GTA 6 is by far the most detailed in the series, with players still discovering secrets in the days after the game's launch. That being said, there have been plenty of sandbox games with large, explorable worlds, such as Cyberpunk 2077 . It takes a special kind of game to hide details within details, making players spend hours exploring one area and still finding rare interactions many others haven't seen. In that regard, GTA 6 is much closer to The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild or Tears of the Kingdom , for how those games shape an open world that feels organic.

When you're going through areas of Leonida in GTA 6 , whether it's a store, gas station, residential area, beach, or other spot, the characters are constantly doing something. Random encounters and constant opportunities for interactions are what help make GTA 6 's world organic, but this wasn't always the case. In games like GTA 4 and GTA 5 , characters in the background felt stale, plastic, and uninteresting. This is what makes the comparison to Breath of the Wild feel even more important, as that was never the case for the characters players interacted with in Hyrule.

The enemies in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom combined with layered map regions full of secrets to unravel. This sometimes meant a dungeon in an unlikely spot, or a civilization full of interesting characters as a small spot on an otherwise huge world map. Packing a sandbox world full of detail seems to be the lesson GTA 6 got from these Nintendo games, with the Rockstar hit never leaving space for players to get bored as they explore. With the Ocarina of Time remake competing with GTA 6 right now too, a Legend of Zelda comparison feels appropriate.

Now, it is true that Sleeping Dogs did release prior to GTA 5 , but Rockstar's title came out less than a year after it. This means that any influence from it wouldn't have been felt at first, as most of the production on GTA 5 in that final year was likely polish and refinement to what had already been developed over the five years since GTA 4 . While mostly another modern world sandbox filled with crime and chaos, Sleeping Dogs is a far different game than any GTA , due to its grittier combat and greater focus on a cohesive narrative inspired by various movies.

The GTA series is no stranger to being influenced by various media, with several Easter Eggs in GTA 6 referencing famous movies and TV shows already. In fact, GTA 3 was almost a carbon copy of Scarface , while The Sopranos was a heavy inspiration for GTA 4 . Sleeping Dogs , though, took many of its story beats from classic Hong Kong action and crime films, with deadly triads and gritty action reflecting a specific style of film instead of a broad stroke. In many ways, Sleeping Dogs was a more violent version of GTA due to how grounded it was, especially compared to the almost cartoonish bloodshed of GTA 5 and GTA Online in that title.

GTA 6 story, by comparison to GTA 5 's, is far more grounded and akin to Sleeping Dogs more than even the other games in its own series. While there is still plenty of GTA 's humor, the tale of Jason and Lucia's struggles has a lot more weight that ditches absurdity for more defined struggles reflective of a movie. Comparisons to Bonny & Clyde , True Romance , and Lethal Weapon are present in GTA 6 , and perhaps the more authentic approach from source material is something Rockstar picked up from Sleeping Dogs and its relationship with Hong Kong cinema.

"What is Shenmue ?" is a question I still ask myself, as the strange but beloved series is something of an enigma even to those who played it. Essentially, Shenmue is a series that is initially about a standard martial arts revenge story, but blossoms into a fully detailed simulation of daily life that many players might find tedious. While 2019's Shemue 3 may be controversial for its lack of modern design features with this concept, the earlier Shenmue games are truly innovative for being the first games to ever immerse players in a "life-sim" approach.

Everything about a Shenmue game is a test of patience, as players have to wait until certain hours of the day to do quests, sometimes participate in getting various chores done, or literally interact with everything in the world. This means opening drawers manually, inspecting various collectibles in detail, or eating/drinking through multiple inputs rather than just one. Combined with some open-world exploration, and this series feels like a more accurate depiction of real life than most games ever get close to. That is, until GTA 6 took the same approach in their incredibly nuanced world design for Leonida.

GTA 6 's world is almost like a fully realized Shenmue , with the fluff and filler of Shenmue 's real-life simulations removed while keeping a focus on daily activities players need to pursue. In Rockstar's game, the first Chapter has you doing chores around the house like manually painting your home, installing new wooden boards, and doing other tasks like picking up groceries to maintain a healthy relationship. Throughout the game, you also have to do things like eat, drink, sleep, go on dates with your partner, and do other activities beyond robbing stores and driving at high speeds down the freeway.

The almost modernization of Shenmue exists through what Rockstar adapted from it, even if it wasn't intentional. The abstract nature of both games encourages players to have pure, unadulterated freedom in spite of clear goals and quests in front of them, making their interactions in the world driven by curiosity rather than linear mandates. Because of that connection, the Shenmue series might be the strongest inspiration for GTA 6 , creating a new standard that games will be trying to catch up to for years to come.

What games and media do you think influenced GTA 6 's direction? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians': How Season 3 Brings Epic Moments to Life and Deals With Annabeth's Absence in the Books
articles.summary: The cast and creatives sat down with THR to talk about adapting the third book in the bestselling series.
articles.content:
Some stories refuse to stay on the page. The Hollywood Reporter’ s Beyond the Book column explores what happens when books make the leap to screen and beyond — unpacking what stayed, changed, how it was done and why it matters with the creatives who made it.

Percy Jackson is back. Season 3 of the Disney+ /Hulu series Percy Jackson and the Olympians continues the saga of the Greek gods, their demigod offspring and the mission to prevent the rise of the Titans.

The storyline is based on The Titan’s Curse , the third book in Rick Riordan 's bestselling series . The plot finds Annabeth Chase (Leah Sava‘ Jeffries) captured by the forces of Kronos, leading Percy (Walker Scobell) to embark on a perilous journey to rescue her. He must free a goddess in chains, confront the Titan’s curse and avoid triggering the fall of Olympus. Co-creator/executive producer Jonathan E. Steinberg tells The Hollywood Reporter that Percy and Annabeth's friendship continues to be central to the story this season.

"In the first two seasons, we were very aware that while we were watching a story about two lonely kids become best friends, there were other things in the offing between them, and that eventually, they would mean more to each other," he says. "Some of that is a romantic story eventually, and some of that is just how best friends they are. Getting to test that and watch them both deal with the idea of losing the other, and maybe never getting them back, is sort of core to the experience of investing in Percy and Annabeth's relationship.“ blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Steinberg praises the season‘s handling of the maturity as "exciting."

"Ultimately, it doesn't matter how tall that monster is, if you don't care about the two people in the center of the story, it's just not going to be exciting. This season really answers both of those calls and doing its work on a grand scale and also putting these people through a trial and interrogating how important they really are to each other," he says.

As the third season rolls out, the cast and creatives — including Scobell, Jeffries, Simhadri, Steinberg and EPs Dan Shotz and Craig Silverstein — sat down to talk with THR about the making of the show, bringing the book's epic moments to life and what fans can expect.

Each season of the show has corresponded with a book in the series. (Season 1 was adapted from 2005's The Lightning Thief, Season 2 from 2006's The Sea of Monsters and now Season 3 from 2007's The Titan's Curse. ) The books feature monsters and battles and mythical creatures, much of which make for an ambitious adaptation to a TV show. For the producers, their challenge is bringing all of that to life.

"Rick doesn't make it easier for us with each book," Shotz quips. "It just gets bigger and bigger as we go. But the benefit of doing a series is you get to keep building and learning from what you did before, and have the show grow."

He gives credit to the entire team for "making this the biggest, best version of itself," including the "massive set pieces." "You want to deliver on kids' imaginations and deliver these creatures, but do it unique to Percy," Shotz adds. "So every time we're trying to build a creature or create a set piece, it's like, what makes it unique to this show? How do you take mythology that's been around for a long time? How do you take what Rick put in his books, and then how do we make it into something that is really special? And it just takes incredible craftsmen and women who just put their best feet forward and deliver on it. The artistry that we got to see this year really felt like it was second to none, and we just went for it." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Silverstein gives credit to Steinberg and Shotz for envisioning something bigger than the small screen. "It starts with the ambition of John and Dan at the outset of this, to say, 'OK, this isn't just the TV version. This is the thing ,'" he shares. "We all love big movies. It's not holding back. These guys really went for it to put this thing up on [a big] scale."

Aryan Simhadri, who plays satyr Grover Underwood, says fans will be pleased this season. "We talk a lot of about the tone shifting, but I'm really proud of how we adapted a lot of the fan-favorite moments from the book," he says. "I think we really did a good job of visualizing these sets and like adapting these moments to screen. It really just looks stunning this season."

Meanwhile, the actors share that they do a deep dive into the books before filming each season. Asked how much they draw on the source material, Jeffries is quick to reply: "Oh, I drew so much."

Scobell offers his own take. "I feel like it's really important to start off every season rereading the book that you're doing," he says. "I reread Book 3 before we went into it and and I've reread Book 2 before we started that [season], and I think that's really important.But at the same time you have to be willing to kind of let some things go because some things are going to get cut, some things are going to get added. It's going change the story a little bit, so you kind of have to keep the core of their character but be willing to change according to the script." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

One of the challenges for the production team is that that the entire book series is a first-person narrative as told by Percy.

"Everything in the book is from Percy's point of view," Silverstein says. "We've long taken the camera off from around his shoulder, and put it out with other people. It's kind of been a slowly widening process of that as the story progresses."

But it's not that easy just to show other characters' points of view without changing the story.

"If the camera cuts to something else that he did not see happen, or someone else he did not see, how does that affect the story of the book?" Silverstein continues. "And in surprising ways, it affects quite a bit. [For example], Percy sees a lot of things through his dreams, but if he doesn't see those things, then the story's ahead of him, and sometimes the audience is ahead of him. Sometimes that's good, and sometimes that's not good. The challenges to the adaptation begin to present themselves, and then you're always trying to steer back to what the core of the story is, what made us excited when we read the books, and hoping that that lines up with what made any reader excited when they read the books."

Annabeth isn't in the third book very much, but she's obviously one of the main characters of the series. For that matter, Clarice (Dior Goodjohn) isn't in it at all — but she also appears in the third season. So how do you tell a story around characters who have little to no presence in the source material? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"It's about taking cues from the book," Silverstein says. "Just because Annabeth's not in the book doesn't mean she's not in the story. She is, and it's about taking the camera to her. We're trying to build the story out. She's up there on Mount Othrys with Luke. Well, what are they talking about? What's going on there? And that's something that colors within the lines of the grand narrative that doesn't change it in a huge way."

As for Clarice, she's not in the book because she's working on a secret mission for Chiron, but it's not clear what that mission is to the reader until later. "If you read the later books, you find out what she's doing," Silvertein adds. "So [in the series], we're going to find out what she's doing a little earlier. Which is what we would have done if we had taken the camera and put it over her shoulder, right? It's fleshing that stuff out."

The producers do consult with Riordan on these types of changes. According to Shotz, the author loves exploring "all these different avenues" as well. "It gives him an opportunity to dive deeper into this world and make suggestions about what he thinks, is happening, that he didn't get to explore when he started this process," Shotz adds.

And, of course, Annabeth is crucial to the overall story. "That's what's amazing about adaptations is, once you have a character like Annabeth, you can't keep telling this story without Leah," Shotz says. "It doesn't work. We must tell her story, so that's really the fun part of it, but also for an audience who's not only going to get their book series honored, but they're going to get all these new things that will excite them. And that makes it really interesting, so that it's not just a book report. You're getting so much more." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For Jeffries, not having source material to draw on actually allowed a bit more freedom in portraying the character. "I really feel like it was kind of up to interpretation for me because I could do a lot of acting improv, not with words but with reactions and how she plays certain scenes, which is a good thing," she says. "It's more of a raw reaction now because when you're playing a part or you're doing a certain scene that's really important in the books, and you know what's in there, it's kind of like you expect it. But with Annabeth and with me especially, it was kind of harder I'm also figuring it out. I wanted to make sure that I still stayed in Annabeth's character, even though she's not in the book [much]." Still, she admits that she was a bit nervous as a result of not having the anything in the books to draw on.

In Season 3, Annabeth also spends much of the story separated from Percy and Grover, which meant Scobell and Simhadri weren't really there to witness Jeffries acting out her scenes, and vice versa. They were only able to see one another's performance once the series started coming together, and they have nothing but praise for one another.

"Once I watched it and saw everything come together — especially you guys, because I wasn't with you guys, so I didn't really get to see what you were doing — you guys looked really good. I'm actually really proud of you guys," Jeffries says.

"it is weird because there were two separate whole stories going on basically at the same time," Scobell adds. "So, not be there for part of it and then see what's going on afterward." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"And to see how much you've grown at the end of the season," Simhadri adds of Annabeth.

Thalia, the demigod daughter of Zeus, has been present throughout the books and series but as a tree for much of the story. In the books, the story goes that Zeus did this to protect her after she sacrificed herself to save her friends. But in a twist, the series diverted from the books; viewers learned in the season finale that he actually transformed her as a punishment after she confronted him about his intentions to use her as a weapon.

She's been mentioned through the books and series up to this point, looming large in the characters' consciousness. We briefly met her in the Season 2 finale after she was transformed back to her human form, but now she's a much bigger part of the story. This season finds Thalia (Tamara Smart) joining forces with Percy, but it's a rocky alliance as he is wary of her loyalty to Luke, the demigod who betrayed Percy way back in Season 1 and has been trying to overthrow the Olympian gods.

"Rick has a phrase about this book, and it applies to this season as well: All of the major chess pieces are coming onto the board," Silverstein says. "Thalia has been talked about since Season 1, but now she's really coming into the story, and when he's talking about the chessboard, what game is it? Well, it's this war between the gods and the Titans. And Thalia is right at the center of all of that. Thalia and Percy and any other potential children of the big three gods who may be out there." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The overall saga of the books comes more into focus in the third book/Season 3, he adds, versus just focusing on "the quest of the year." "And what Thalia decides to do will affect not just all of the people she loves and her friends, but the entire world and all of her parents and all of her grandparents," he adds. "She's got a big role."

As for how the dynamic changes with Thalia around, the actors say it introduces a rivalry between the characters. Simhadri begins, "We all wanted to be — " "the biggest and baddest," Jeffries finishes as he nods. (The cast often finishes each other's sentences.) Scobell expands: "Thalia is kind of in competition with Percy for his spot in that kind of group. But she can't just show up and join us. It's not like [Percy's cyclops half-brother] Tyson, where he and Grover can exist. There can be only one." Simhaddri echoes that sentiment: "It's one or the other."

Percy has arguably the biggest growth of any character up to this point, as he started off the series thinking he was a regular boy before learning he was a demigod and becoming a hero.

"The most important part about playing Perseus Jackson is also experiencing my own life in the same way," Scobell says. "He goes to camp every summer and then he goes back to school and back to his real life. I do the same thing. We take a big break in between every season."

But now, Scobell finishing his last year in high school and still awaiting word on a fourth season. "So I'm kind of moving into uncharted territory because before, I could look forward to next season and really just be comfortable going to school and living my own life, but this is going to be a big change for me because it's so uncertain." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For Simhadri, he also felt like Grover grew a lot of over the course of the season, as did he, not only as a person but as an actor. "I was an adult on season 2, but I never ended up working that many hours per day," he shares. "But in season 3, I was back every day filming and I was working with a ton of adults, so we would all just shoot for as long as we could in well into the night and really just like push ourselves every day. So I feel like not only did Grover grow over the course of the season, I think I grew in tandem alongside him."

This year has seen not only more Percy Jackson but also the box office blockbuster The Odyssey. Why are people suddenly gaga over the Greek gods?

"It's timeless," Steinberg says. "Those stories have evolved to be about universal experiences that just kind of live really deeply in everybody. I think it's really not surprising that they never quite go away, because they apply to everybody. We're happy that it's in the zeitgeist, but not surprised."

"And Percy did it a lot faster than Odysseus," Shotz quips of the latter's 20-year journey back home.

articles.title: DC's Weirdest Hero Was Created by Spider-Man's Co-Creator, and His Forgotten Legacy Is Stranger Than You Think

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Steve Ditko is one of the most important creators in the history of the comic industry. Working for Atlas Comics in the '50s, he would become an important part of Marvel's return to superheroes. He's most known as the co-creator of Spider-Man and Doctor Strange , working with writer Stan Lee, but he also had quite a career outside the House of Ideas. Over at Charlton Comics, he created characters like Ted Kord, the second Blue Beetle, Captain Atom, and the Question and would also have a pretty fruitful tenure with DC Comics as well. He created the Creeper, a psychotic television host vigilante, the teen duo Hawk and Dove, and one more character you've probably never head of – Shade the Changing Man.

Ditko characters often went in certain directions – many of them shared his Randian belief system (it's always fun to read early libertarian Peter Parker) or were all about finding the "truth" like the Question and the Creeper. Shade, though, was quite different from all of the rest. Rac Shade was an alien from the planet Meta (unrelated to the Zuck), on the run from the militant authorities and armed with the M-Vest. Shade was a rare foray into sci-fi for Ditko and while the hero never really caught on back in the day, he's had a rich second life, playing a bigger role in the history of the comic industry than most fans realize.

Ditko's characters may not have all been Objectivist (a libertarian belief system that posits that the individual's job isn't to help the collective, but just themselves), but all of them had a certain "fight the power" feel to them. Shade the Changing Man is a perfect example of this. Rac came from a Meta, a world where the rules were followed to a militant degree. He was a secret agent who was eventually framed for treason, stealing the M-Vest and heading to Earth where he could be free.

The M-Vest allowed Shade to create powerful forcefields and make himself into a bigger, more monstrous fighter. The character first debuted in 1977, representing the first major superhero Ditko had created in years, but wasn't a massive hit. The first series ran for eight issues before folding, with Shade joining the army of obscure DC characters. In the '80s, he would end up showing up as a member of the Suicide Squad, which lead to him going back to Meta. However, things were about to look all the way up.

Sidetrack time! In 1982, British writer Alan Moore was given the reins of Saga of the Swamp Thing after years of success in British comic magazines like 2000 A.D. and Warrior . Moore's Swamp Thing took superhero comics in a more mature direction , starting a revolution that would lead DC to decide that the British comic scene was home to a lot of untapped talent. As the '80s went on, DC bigwigs Jenette Kahn, Paul Levitz, and Dick Giordano would meet with British talent, leading to the British Invasion of 1989.

Writers Neil Gaiman, Grant Morrison, and Peter Milligan were the first big gets of this program and each of them were given their choice of obscure DC character to write. Gaiman chose Black Orchid (with his accent, the editor thought he said "Black Hawk Kid", as related in The Sandman Companion ; I was once a massive fan of the writer before the allegations came out), Morrison Animal Man, and Milligan would go with Shade. It's weird to think that the entire comic industry was changed forever because of Animal Man, Black Orchid, and Shade the Changing Man

Shade the Changing Man (Vol. 2) dropped in 1990, from Milligan and future X-Men superstar artist Chris Bachalo. Instead of being a secret agent, this new Rac Shade was a poet sent from Meta, now more hippie than militant, to save Earth from a tide of madness that threatened to destroy the planet. The M-Vest was now the Madness Vest, which could warp reality and his first major enemy was the American Scream, the living embodiment of the darkness that Rac was sent to fight. The secret agent was gone, replaced by a lovelorn poet.

It's always interesting to see how creators take old ideas and remake them. Ditko's beliefs usually got left out of the characters he created as the years went by, the new Rac Shade was basically the completely different from the old one; in fact, you could say that he was meant to be a critique on Ditko and his belief system (Milligan retconned Ditko's Meta by having Rac say it was all stuff he made up to entertain himself while he was on Earth). Meta was remade from the Cold War nightmare into something more akin to the Summer of Love (the one in the '90s, not the one in the '60s; some of you know what I'm talking about and some of you are much too American to know the pop culture of other countries) and suddenly, Rac was all about helping people and making their lives better. Much like Morrison, Milligan was plugged into the rave culture of the time and Shade the Changing Man played into this.

The book dealt with subjects like the JFK assassination (we were obsessed with the JFK assassination in the '90s) and transgender issues (Milligan's Enigma is a lost queer history gem), and its subject matter and the more mature way it and the other British Invasion comics were written led to DC creating the Vertigo imprint in 1993. Shade never reached the level of popularity or The Sandman, Hellblazer, Animal Man, Swamp Thing or Doom Patrol , but it had a cult following, the book running for 70 issues.

DC tried to bring Shade back as a superhero character several times over the years after the end of the Vertigo series to no avail, which would lead to another modification of the character. In 2016, DC announced the Young Animal imprint from My Chemical Romance singer/comic mega-fan Gerard Way and one of the inaugural books was Shade the Changing Girl . This version combined aspects of both – Meta was a world where emotion was punished and poet Loma Shade stole the Madness Vest and went to Earth – and ran through two series, the first for 12 issues and the second, titled Shade the Changing Woman , running for six.

Steve Ditko's place as a Marvel legend is cemented, but his time outside that publisher doesn't get as much mainstream recognition. His DC creations are some of his most interesting and Shade the Changing Man was a cool idea that proved to have longer legs than his initial eight-issue offering led readers to believe. His return in the late '80s as a part of the British Invasion proved that failures didn't always happen because the ideas are bad – they just need a little push (to the left; there's a moral there).

Shade the Changing Man (Vol. 2) pushed the envelope, playing a huge role in the rise of Vertigo at DC . While he was never at the level of someone like John Constantine or Animal Man or Dream of the endless, Rac played an important role in the evolution of the medium. Milligan doesn't get the praise that Morrison gets or that Gaiman used to but he definitely deserves it. His re-imagining of Shade took a character that didn't have a chance and made him groundbreaking.

What do you think about Shade the Changing Man? Do you the Ditko original or are you more into the Vertigo version? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: Jennifer Lopez Just Wore A Necklace So Rare It Needed Its Own Security Detail
articles.summary: It’s hard not to be distracted by this rock that Jenny on the Block has got.
articles.content:
Jennifer Lopez is a global icon and movie star. She is also celebrating the Thanksgiving release of her concert film The JLo Show, on the 2026 TV schedule , by making a splash at the red carpet premiere and showing off a necklace that needed its own security detail. Few celebrities could pull off a 186-carat diamond necklace and not feel as though the jewelry were overpowering them, and yet J. Lo manages to somehow do so with ease.

Very few people in the world could see an ensemble and jewelry of that caliber and say, “I love those,” and then find themselves wearing them mere months later, but that seems to be exactly what happened, according to Variety . While the coat was a gift, the necklace was on loan and came with a four-person security detail that included two armed off-duty police officers.

The superstar has had quite the 2026. JLo’s rom-com Office Romance was a No. 1 hit on Netflix , her twins graduated high school and headed off to college, and she’s been enjoying the single life . Now, she’s peeling the curtain back to give audiences a glimpse into her Caesars Palace residency in Las Vegas with The JLo Show . The special not only captures her performing some of her iconic hits, but it also chronicles her life, from growing up in the Bronx to becoming who she is today.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The studio behind Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba is currently taking over theaters in Japan with a new movie hitting the big screen, and it's going all out to celebrate the occasion with a new look at Witch on the Holy Night. Studio Ufotable has been keeping very busy over the last couple of years as while fans are waiting to see what's next for the Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle trilogy , the studio has gone ahead and released a new feature film in the meantime.

Witch on the Holy Night is the next major TYPE-MOON franchise release that Ufotable has helped to bring to life over the last few years, and it's set before the events of any of the Fate/stay night universe projects seen before. It's now tearing its way through theaters across Japan, and it's going all out to commemorate the occasion with a new trailer and poster helping to show it off as it expands to Screen X and other formats in the region. Check them out below.

Witch on the Holy Night originally made its debut in Japan this past weekend, but thankfully it won't be too long before fans in North America get their chance to see it in action for themselves. Crunchyroll and Sony Pictures Entertainment will be releasing the new film in the United States, Canada and more international territories on January 29th next yea r with both Japanese and English dubbed audio releases planned. If you've seen any of the TYPE-MOON projects before, this one is likely going to ring some bells.

Witch on the Holy Night is based off of the TYPE-MOON visual novel originally written by Kinoko Nasu , the same creator behind the massive Fate/stay night franchise. Directed by Masashi Takeuchi for ufotable with Moe Tsuzuki providing the character designs, Manabu Kamino handling the editing, and Hideyuki Fukasawa composing the music, it's also going to feature the theme song titled "Yoru to Ao" as performed by supercell. Even if you don't have experience with Nasu's prior works, this is still a suitable entry point.

Witch on the Holy Night is a prequel story that takes place before the events of releases like Tsukihime and more that have already gotten their own anime adaptations in the past. The Japanese voice cast from the original light novel release are set to reprise their roles with the likes of Haruka Tomatsu as Aoko Aozaki, Kana Hanazawa as Alice Kuonji, and Yusuke Kobayashi as Soujyuro Shizuki, but the potential English voice cast has yet to be revealed as of this time.

With this story not really tied to anything else, it's not really going to require any homework to jump into Witch on the Holy Night . Naturally it is going to have a bigger impact on those fans who are experienced with the previously released works, but at least those who just want to see Ufotable's next movie won't have to worry too much. Which is even better without a new Demon Slayer entry this year . Are you going to check out Witch on the Holy Night when you get the chance? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Two Of My Favorite Hallmark Actors Are Finally In A Movie Together And I’m Obsessed
articles.summary: Get these two in more movies ASAP!
articles.content:
Hallmark churns out nearly a hundred new romance movies every year. The 2026 Countdown to Christmas lineup alone is slated for 34 original holiday-themed flicks. Part of the reason it’s easy for the cable channel-turned-streamer to make so many movies a year is that it has a list of dedicated actors who are eager to star in these films -- like Queen of Hallmark Lacey Chabert . And yet, somehow, they manage to keep the pairings fresh. So fresh that two of my favorite longtime Hallmark actors, Erin Cahill and Andrew Walker, just starred in their first movie together. I’m happy to report it was worth the wait!

The residents of Blue Dog Valley aren’t too thrilled about an outsider taking over their beloved veterinary practice, and Goldie has to work overtime to win over the hearts of the town’s loyal pet owners. Desperate for an ally, Goldie turns to Cohen (Walker), the son of the former owner of the vet practice, for help. While they get off to a rough start, sparks start to fly as the two spend more time together, especially with Goldie taking over planning duties for the annual Christmas parade that will feature the four-legged and furry residents of the town this year.

It can be easy for the human actors to get upstaged by their animal co-stars , especially when there are so many different types of animals in a movie (cows, alpacas, and of course dogs in this case), but Cahill and Walker managed to hold things down even in the face of an adorable, overweight corgi. It’s a testament to the chemistry these two have on screen.

articles.title: The Dragonborn Could Return in The Elder Scrolls 6, But Not in the Way Players Expect
articles.summary: Fans have managed to glean a lot about The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel after the game's brief title drop earlier this month, with a short video being surprisingly full of useful information. We can now confirm the game's setting based on the title, and surprisingly, we also got a hint towards when in the franchise's […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Fans have managed to glean a lot about The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel after the game's brief title drop earlier this month, with a short video being surprisingly full of useful information. We can now confirm the game's setting based on the title, and surprisingly, we also got a hint towards when in the franchise's timeline the game takes place. It is precisely because of this hint that players can expect the possibility of the Dragonborn returning in The Elder Scrolls 6 , though it might not be in the way you might expect.

In case you've been living under a rock for the last 15 years, the Dragonborn is the title used to refer to the player character of The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim . Known as Dovahkiin in the language of the dragons, the Dragonborn is a mortal gifted with the blood and soul of a dragon, and the ability to consume their souls to learn dragon shouts. While several Dragonborn have exited throughout The Elder Scroll 's history, Skyrim's protagonist plays a particularly important role in prophecy, as well as the politics of the fourth era, having a vital role in determining the victor of Skyrim's civil war and helping to determine the fates of Aldmeri Dominion plots and the stability of the weakened empire.

From the trailer for The Elder Scrolls 6 , we can tell that the aftermath of the last great war plays a huge part in the story of the game. Particularly, the Aldmeri Dominion's failed invasion of Hammerfell and the continuing war that the Redguard states fought against the Dominion, which ultimately led to Dominion forces retreating from Hammerfell's shores.

Not only are these events likely to play an important role in the game's story, but according to the trailer, The Elder Scrolls 6 takes place less than ten years after the events of Skyrim . Because of the Dragonborn's importance to the events preceding and defined by the Great War, and the close proximity on the timeline, there is a good chance that they'll be making an appearance in The Elder Scrolls 6. However, chances are we won't actually get to meet them.

We can already be sure that players won't be playing the Dragonborn in TES6, with a new power taking the place of dragon shouts. However, with the Dragonborn's importance to the events occurring in the game, we'll likely see the Dragonborn in flashbacks, an introduction cutscene at the start of the game, or mentioned by NPCs.

If we don't end up seeing the Dragonborn in any cutscenes, we can be sure that the character will be mentioned in conservation at least once over the course of the game. Any NPC mentioning news about the civil war in Skyrim, the dragon attacks, which easily could have made their way to Hammerfell, or the fate of the Empire is sure to mention word of intervention from a mysterious prisoner who was bound for the execution block but upended the entire region with the power of the voice.

Stories of the Dragonborn may also be used to inspire the native Redguard in their own civil war or an impending second Dominion invasion. Bethesda may even go so far as to shape dialogue depending on the choices you made in Skyrim , a system that many RPG sequels are known to do.

While chances are high that the Dragonborn will be mentioned in The Elder Scrolls 6 , we can assume with a degree of certainty that the Dragonborn themselves won't actually make a physical appearance in the game, at least outside of potential cutscenes or flashbacks.

There are several reasons why this isn't practical, but the biggest one is pretty simple: The Dragonborn was a player character. With Skyrim being an open-world game that allows players to customize their character completely, it becomes almost impossible to create an NPC model in The Elder Scrolls 6 that conveys the look of your Dragonborn, without actually taking information from your Skyrim saved game.

While Bethesda has used a somewhat generic Nord look to represent the Dragonborn in promotional material, it just wouldn't be satisfying to try and convince players that they were speaking to the living, breathing Dragonborn, when so much of Skyrim's appeal was shaped by how you chose to play. If your Dragonborn was an Argonian mage or a Dunmer assassin aligned with the Dark Brotherhood, coming face-to-face with a heavily armored Nord claiming to be your old character would just be insulting.

Do you think the Dragonborn will make an appearance in The Elder Scrolls 6 ? Do you think the games should be further apart on the timeline? Leave your answers in the comments below.

articles.title: Star Wars: David Fincher Reveals Movie He Pitched to Lucasfilm, And the Two Characters It Followed
articles.summary: Lucasfilm The Star Wars franchise has had a rocky time since Disney acquired the franchise. After a massively successful relaunch with Star Wars: The Force Awakens, the franchise hit turbulence that lasted for nearly half a decade, as sequel trilogy films like The Last Jedi divided audiences, while the entire planned line of Star Wars "standalones" […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Star Wars franchise has had a rocky time since Disney acquired the franchise. After a massively successful relaunch with Star Wars: The Force Awakens , the franchise hit turbulence that lasted for nearly half a decade, as sequel trilogy films like The Last Jedi divided audiences, while the entire planned line of Star Wars "standalones" fizzled out after films like Rogue One and Solo failed to be the kind of hits the studio wanted. However, in the early 2010s, before Disney came in, rumors swirled about different filmmakers taking meetings with Lucasfilm, pitching their own concepts for Star Wars standalones that would've expanded the franchise's creative palette.

One of the directors involved in that mix was David Fincher , the acclaimed director of films like Fight Club, Se7en, and Gone Girl . In a new interview, Fincher goes into a lot more depth about what his pitch for a Star Wars movie was all about, as well as revealing the game-changing business advice he gave Lucasfilm head Kathleen Kennedy, just before the Disney acquisition.

David Fincher was speaking with Josh Horowitz on his Happy Sad Confused podcast , and was ready to speak more in-depth about what he wanted to do with his Star Wars movie. The long and short of it is that Fincher wanted to explore Star Wars and the events of the original trilogy from the perspective of the droids who were caught in the middle of it.

"I have a very personal relationship to Star Wars, obviously, because I was stealing storyboards out of the garbage cans at Lucasfilm in 1975. And I knew Ralph McQuarrie," Fincher explained. "Here's what I was interested in; here's what I pitched Kathy [Kennedy]: I said, 'The thing that has always interested me about – certainly from the first movie – was the relationship between [C-]3PO and R2-D2. That they were essentially slaves who would bear witness to the folly of man. And I always thought, them being captured by Jawas, and then sold off and being on the periphery and witnessing the Skywalker Saga, was such a crucial element to it, that I really felt had gotten away from this kind… of moral judgement."

Fincher went even deeper, lamenting how Star Wars has largely squandered the opportunity to use its droid characters in more serious ways. He clearly had a sci-fi angle on how the robotic beings interpreted the fight between light and dark side Force users like the Jedi and Sith, or the geopolitics that pushed things towards multiple cycles of galactic war. Fincher's film would apparently have examined a record of the Skywalker Saga and Galactic Civil War, which was stored inside a droid like C-3PO, and offer a new artificial intelligence perspective on it all.

"I mean, it was fairly obvious even from 3PO, whose politics at his worst, you could say… he had a kind of understanding as to what the Empire meant… how evil they were. And he was kind of trying to decide whether or not he wanted to invest in having a relationship with Luke Skywalker when he's getting his oil bath, and they're talking about [it]. And I always thought that… whenever they used the robots for that, I was always really excited. I always thought that was kind of an interesting thing that you kind of go through the recorder, like the court reporter, to find out what it is that happened."

Ironically, Star Wars comics would repurpose the idea of how droids view being servants to the warring and self-destructive cycles of organic lifeforms in the 2023 story arc, "Dark Droids". A droid A.I. and Sith relic known as the "Spark Eternal" combined to create "The Scourge," a self-aware AI able to possess other droids and machines as part of its hive consciousness. C-3PO was one of the first and primary host bodies Scourge used to conduct its experiments with possessing organics with its machine consciousness. The villain gave hell to both the Rebellion and Empire before finally being defeated. It was a compelling story, which lends credit to the fact that Fincher's film would've been one, as well. But fate had other plans:

"So that's what we had started talking about, and then I said to her [Kathleen Kennedy], 'I kind of pictured this idea.' I said, 'Let's take this thing to Wall Street and let the market decide. And I think it was a month later or something, she said, 'Bad news. Apparently there's a $7 billion offer on the table,' and I said, 'I don't think – we're not going to beat that [laughs].'"

Disney ended the wild, creative-driven possibilities for Star Wars and locked into recycled nostalgia. And now it's doubtful that a film like Fincher's will ever get made, as Disney is shifting back to crowd-pleasing blockbusters, like Ryan Gosling's upcoming film, Star Wars: Starfighter .

articles.title: Wedding Surprise: Casey Wasserman and Jenny Chandler Reveal Marriage at Friendsgiving-Turned-Reception: "Best. Night. Ever"
articles.summary: The bride confirmed the news in an Instagram video that featured an inside look at the reception, billed as "The Greatest Gathering": "What a magical night, surrounded by so much LOVE!"
articles.content:
Casey Wasserman is a married man.

The veteran Hollywood mogul, who is steering the ship for the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028 as chairman, married longtime girlfriend, Jenny Chandler. The couple revealed the news last week at their Los Angeles home where they hosted approximately 200 guests for what was billed as a Friendsgiving celebration only later to be unveiled as a wedding reception.

"Best. Night. Ever. 💞✨," Chandler shared on Instagram Sunday, confirming news that had first been reported by Page Six Hollywood's editor Ian Mohr. The post included a video from inside the event showing an elaborate setting under a massive tent with tables for dinner, white candles, a sign that read "The Greatest Gathering" as a play on the film The Greatest Showman. articles.title: Netflix's One Piece Anime Remake Shares New Look Ahead of 2027 Debut
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of WIT Studio With only a few months left before the premiere of One Piece's anticipated anime remake, fans get a new look at Luffy and Koby. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With only a few months left before the premiere of One Piece 's anticipated anime remake, fans get a new look at Luffy and Koby. It's been almost three years since Netflix's One Piece remake by WIT Studio was officially announced , and fans have been anticipating the series ever since. The manga began serialization in 1997, and the anime has been ongoing since 1998, making One Piece one of the longest-running franchises of all time. However, beginners would often get overwhelmed with the anime having more than a thousand episodes, which made it even more difficult for the series to get new fans.

The historic success of the live-action adaptation confirmed that anime enthusiasts would be more than willing to follow Luffy's epic journey if only the series weren't more than a thousand episodes long. This is why a remake was announced to attract new fans and give the series a modern adaptation . While the anime is still a few months away, ScreenRant shared a new look at Luffy and Koby in an exclusive Winter TV preview. The visual features the duo sailing in a boat, which means it's set in the time before they ran into Zoro.

ScreenRant’s 2026-27 Winter TV Preview presents The One Piece. 🏴‍☠️ Eiichiro Oda's manga is getting a fresh adaptation on Netflix that will take viewers back to the beginning of Monkey D. Luffy's adventure in search of the "One Piece" treasure alongside his new crew. The first… pic.twitter.com/2dheThzLDU

The One Piece will premiere with Netflix in February 2027 as part of the Winter 2027 lineup, but the exact release date hasn't been revealed yet. The One Piece has revealed its teaser , official character designs, and key visuals, but fans still await a full-length trailer featuring everything we need to know before the premiere. We can expect more updates during Jump Festa 2027, which will be held on December 19th and 20th later this year.

As the biggest Shonen Jump manga of all time, One Piece will be holding a panel at the Super Stage where it will drop new updates regarding its ongoing and upcoming projects. Fans can expect more information, including a release date and a trailer for the remake during the convention. The remake will be streaming exclusively on Netflix worldwide, and has already confirmed that the first season will have seven episodes. All of which are expected to drop on the same day.

The biggest issue fans face in the original anime is the slow pacing, which is caused by the weekly schedule over the years. While the anime adapted a seasonal schedule starting from the Elbaph Arc of the Final Saga, each episode is still adapting only one chapter, which is considerably slow-paced. The remake will adapt the first 50 chapters of the manga in seven episodes, each spanning a little more than 40 minutes. The first season will adapt the East Blue Saga, where Luffy begins his journey and forms a crew to travel all the way to the Grand Line.

The first season will feature up to the Baratie Arc, although it’s uncertain if the entire arc will be covered. At the very least, it's confirmed that Sanji will be introduced in the first season, along with the rest of the East Blue crew. Additionally, we will need the anime to premiere first before knowing if there will be more seasons going forward. Considering how long One Piece is, the remake will need several more seasons if it plans to adapt the entire story.

Are you excited for the highly anticipated One Piece remake? Which favorite moment do you want to revisit in the new adaptation? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: Super Bowl LXI to Touch Down in Imax Theaters
articles.summary: The NFL, ESPN and Walt Disney have agreed a first-ever deal to live stream the ultimate sports championship game in large format theaters in domestic and select international markets.
articles.content:
ESPN, Walt Disney and the National Football League have agreed a first-time deal to see Super Bowl LXI broadcast live on the big screen in Imax theaters in the U.S. and select international markets.

With Super Bowl LXI the first for ESPN in the sport media brand's history, its four-hour game day telecast on Feb. 14, 2027 will feature the main championship game telecast, the halftime show headlined by Jay-Z and pregame and postgame coverage.

The Imax partnership is part of an effort by Walt Disney to make the 2027 Super Bowl telecast as widely accessible as possible. “Watching the Super Bowl with your fellow fans is one of the great shared experiences in sports, and this first-of-its-kind collaboration with the NFL and Imax takes it to a historic new scale,” Ken Potrock, president, major event integration for The Walt Disney Company, said in a statement on Monday.

“With ESPN’s first Super Bowl, we’re reaching fans across an unprecedented range of platforms and meeting them wherever they want to be, with unique moments that only Disney and ESPN can deliver," he added. Walt Disney plans to leverage every part of its portfolio, from theme parks to films to products and experiences to drive awareness to the 2027 Super Bowl game.

In an era of 70-inch TV screens and sporting events in sports bar, the NFL is also looking to bring its game day live event product to even bigger screens, with food and beverages on sale in the lobby. The NFL in 2017 struck a sponsorship deal with Canadian cinema giant Cineplex to show Sunday Night Football and the Super Bowl broadcast live on its movie screens north of the U.S. border.

And Cinemark recently unveiled plans to bring a Monday Night Football game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Seattle Seahawks on Dec. 7 to a first-ever in-market NFL watch party at its theater in West Plano, Texas, as part of another sponsorship deal. NFL games are currently shown in COSM venues as well.

“The Super Bowl is a one-of-a-kind global cultural event imbued with spectacle, sound, drama, and heroes — all the makings of a great Imax experience,” Rich Gelfond, CEO of Imax said in his own statement. “This is a milestone for Imax that further elevates our standing as a premier global platform for entertainment and events, and we’re excited to work in partnership with Disney, ESPN and the NFL to give football fans an unforgettable night.”

The Super Bowl LXI game telecast promises to be the largest live event ever for Imax as its large format theaters in Australia, New Zealand and Brazil will also broadcast the championship NFL game.

As the NFL looks to broaden its international audience, including on more digital platforms, ESPN earlier announced additional content like Super Bowl LXI with Peyton and Eli (ESPN2), Super Bowl LXI Field Pass with The Pat McAfee Show (ESPNU), Super Bowl LXI Playbook with Next Gen Stats (NFL Network), and the first-ever Star Wars Funday Football animated telecast on Disney+, Disney Channel and Disney XD.

ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcast team of Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Lisa Salters and Laura Rutledge will call the Super Bowl LXI game.

EXCLUSIVE: Early on the morning of February 2, 2022, a police SWAT team in Minneapolis burst into an apartment on a no-knock warrant. Within 10 seconds, an officer had fatally shot a young Black man who had been sleeping on the couch, 22-year-old Amir Locke.

That shocking incident and the family’s fight for justice is explored in the Oscar-contending documentary No Knock - No Charge? The Amir Locke Story , directed by Andrew Niccademous Tyler . The film opens Friday for a one-week run at the Laemmle Noho 7 in North Hollywood, CA.

Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison, the Hennepin County district attorney and other authorities announced in April 2022 they would not seek charges against the officer who fired on Locke, a controversial decision that triggered protests in Minneapolis-St. Paul, Chicago and other cities.

Amir Locke was not an object of the no-knock warrant; he was staying in the apartment of his cousin, who was a suspect in a homicide. articles.title: I’ve Wondered If Bari Weiss’ CBS News Will Merge With CNN. Someone Asked Skydance’s Head Honcho
articles.summary: This is CNN... and CBS News?
articles.content:
The merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery has resulted in the formation of Skydance, which now holds various high-profile media assets. From a news perspective, the David Ellison-led conglomerate now owns both CBS News and CNN. There’s been a considerable amount of discussion regarding the future of both entities, especially in regard to whether CBS’ Bari Weiss might run CNN. While Weiss won’t take that big seat , I’ve still been curious about a merger, and Ellison recently weighed in.

So this answer pretty much seems to fall into the category of “not a definitive yes, but not a definitive no”. At the very least, the possibility of “news sharing” does make sense due to the two networks now being under the same corporate umbrella. I still can’t help but wonder, however, whether Ellison isn't totally shutting down the merger idea due to it being internally discussed as a viable option. That’s just speculation on my part, of course, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the powers that be have or are currently pondering the idea, at the very least.

Ellison eventually confirmed this past October, however, that current CNN CEO Mark Thompson would remain in his post. Shortly thereafter, Thompson spoke about the merger and shared some complimentary thoughts on his new bosses. The CEO said that after speaking to Ellison and the other Skydance executives, he felt “real confidence that they both understand and will fully support the principle and practice of the kind of independent news that CNN has always stood for.” All in all, Thompson has a solid reputation, and former CBS anchor Scott Pelley also praised him while warning CNN staffers about possible editorial changes post-merger.

articles.summary: The whole world is talking about Grand Theft Auto VI now that it has finally arrived. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The whole world is talking about Grand Theft Auto VI now that it has finally arrived. As great and engaging as the game's main story is, one of the most fun aspects is learning that millions of players all over the world are discovering the incredible number of easter eggs sprinkled throughout the map. So far, people have explored the massive map and encountered some wild events. There's a dog that rides a jet ski and saves you from being stranded in the water, you can find nods to Dexter and Fast and the Furious , you can end up in an actual trap right out of the Saw franchise, and more.

With so many references to notable pieces of pop culture, it makes sense that Marvel Comics is part of that. Like many of the other easter eggs in Grand Theft Auto VI , you likely won't go off looking for anything specifically related to Marvel, yet there are a few. So far, just days after the game's initial launch, there have been two nods to Marvel Comics that people have stumbled upon, including one that references the MCU. Of course, there could likely be a bunch more that players haven't found quite yet.

The easiest reference to find in Grand Theft Auto VI related to Marvel is the RX-Men comic book. Throughout the game, there are dozens of magazines and comics for you to collect, including one about the RX-Men, which is clearly a parody of the X-Men. You can actually open and read the story, which turns the characters into pharmaceutical jokes. Dr. Placebo is the main villain, acting as a mix of Dr. Doom and Magneto. Meanwhile, the heroes include Side Effect, Capsule, Diagnosis, and Mr. I (a play on MRI). The comic can be found at the 24-hour convenience store near your initial home in Key Lento.

The more surprising and in-depth Marvel reference is harder to find, featuring a creature who feels a lot like the Red Hulk. It all starts soon after Chapter 1, when, as Lucia, you find a flyer for a "pilot wanted" at the Starlet Motel's reception area. That will give you Kyle's number and you start doing side jobs for him involving chemicals. When you reach Chapter 3, you get a strange text from Kyle and investigate at his farm. Once there, you head to the back of the barn, which is surrounded by agents. Suddenly, Kyle bursts out as a chemically mutated creature who resembles the Red Hulk.

The moment was first famously found by streamer IShowSpeed and all of his viewers were just as shocked as he was. Kyle might not look exactly like Red Hulk, but he's massive, red, and ripping out of his clothes. The reference even goes far enough to show him throw someone into a helicopter, which is a scene pulled straight out of Captain America: Brave New World . You don't have to fight Kyle either, as you can just sit back and watch the carnage unfold from the side. Hopefully, there are even more Marvel references waiting to be found.

articles.title: Does GTA 6’s Infinite Money Glitch Still Work After Today’s Patch? Here's What We Know
articles.summary: Not long after its release this past week, Grand Theft Auto 6 players quickly discovered an exploit that allowed them to earn endless money. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Not long after its release this past week, Grand Theft Auto 6 players quickly discovered an exploit that allowed them to earn endless money. This workaround was one that many quickly took advantage of for themselves, as it was assumed that Rockstar would quickly look to resolve this oversight with a new update. And while the first post-launch update for GTA 6 is now out , it seems that Rockstar hasn't patched this infinite money glitch after all.

As of this moment, update version 1.002.002 for Grand Theft Auto 6 is live across PS5 and Xbox platforms. The main purpose of this update has been to fix a number of bugs and other errors that players have come across in their time playing so far. Naturally, this would make one think that the infinite money exploit would be one of the most prominent bugs squashed with this update, but that hasn't been the case at all. Instead, Rockstar has resolved issues relating to autosaving, the weather system, and another with the game's phone feature. Any mention of this infinite money glitch being resolved has been found nowhere in the patch notes for the update, which means that it should still work at the time of this writing.

On a long enough timeline, Rockstar will almost certainly end up squashing this endless money loophole in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Today's patch represents the first of countless updates for the game that will roll out in the weeks, months, and years to come. Over time, this glitch will undoubtedly end up being rectified, so players shouldn't expect it to stick around forever.

Perhaps the biggest reason why Rockstar hasn't resolved this money glitch in GTA 6 just yet is because it somewhat betrays the entire purpose of the game . Since money is more important in GTA 6 than in any other Grand Theft Auto entry, the process of earning cash is meant to be a grind for players as they push to build up their savings and checking accounts. To betray this grind by taking advantage of an exploit will only diminish Grand Theft Auto 6 for many players, even if they believe otherwise. For this reason, it might be why Rockstar isn't in any rush to fix this bug immediately, as those using the bug in the first place are only making the game worse.
